question: Refer to the exhibit. A VXLAN data center fabric consists of three hosts mapped to different VLANs. Ingress VTEPs perform Layer 2 bridging and Layer 3 routing. Egress VTEPs only perform a Layer 2 bridging lookup. Which VNI values must be set to allow inter-VNI communication?
context: Topology: Spine1 connects to Leaf1 (Host-1, IP 192.168.1.1/24, VRF Test_Telco, VLAN 100), Leaf2 (Host-2, IP 192.168.2.1/24, VRF Test_Telco, VLAN 200), and Leaf3/Leaf4 (S1, IP 192.168.3.1/24, VRF Test_Telco, VLAN 300, VNI 1010).
imageNote: Diagram: Spine1 connects to Leaf1 (Host-1, VLAN100), Leaf2 (Host-2, VLAN200), and Leaf3/Leaf4 (S1, VLAN300/VNI1010), all in VRF Test_Telco.
options: VLAN 100 to Layer 2 VNI 2020 - Test_Telco_VRF to Layer 3 VNI 5050
VLAN 100 to Layer 2 VNI 2020 - VLAN 200 to Layer 2 VNI 5050
VLAN 100 to Layer 2 VNI 2020 - Test_Telco_VRF to Layer 3 VNI 1010
VLAN 100 to Layer 2 VNI 1010 - VLAN 200 to Layer 2 VNI 1010
theory: The scenario describes asymmetric Integrated Routing and Bridging: because the egress VTEP only performs a Layer 2 bridging lookup rather than routing, the ingress VTEP must both route the packet into the destination's Layer 2 segment and encapsulate it directly with the destination VLAN's own Layer 2 VNI. This only works if every VTEP in the fabric has all the relevant Layer 2 VNIs locally configured, since there is no shared Layer 3 transit VNI involved, unlike symmetric IRB, which routes through a common VRF-wide Layer 3 VNI and lets every VTEP perform both bridging and routing — which is why answers referencing a shared Layer 3 VNI don't match the asymmetric behavior described here. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 3 — VXLAN EVPN Asymmetric vs. Symmetric IRB)
